subject: Procurement & Pricing Next Steps — Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood-inference.com>
To: Samantha Reynolds <samantha.reynolds@acme.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood-inference.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood-inference.com>, Michael Grant <michael@redwood-inference.com>
Date: 2026-10-12T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Recap & Next Steps from Today’s Discovery — Procurement and Packaging Options

Hi Samantha —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps to keep procurement moving: 

Summary of what we heard:
- Pilot scope: PoC for chat and embeddings on ~250k messages/month (expected burst to 500k).
- Latency target: 200–400ms p50 for chat.
- Data residency: US-only for now.
- Procurement preference: typically PO through central purchasing; card is only for small one-off buys.
- Interest in Marketplace for simplified procurement, but team needs pricing that supports a 12–24 month commit if we go Dedicated.

Recommended commercial path (to match purchasing rules):
1) Start with Hosted (Redwood API, hosted) for the 6–8 week pilot — fastest time-to-value, no infra onboarding.
2) If pilot meets SLA/scale, transition to Dedicated capacity for production to get predictable throughput and unit economics. Dedicated supports monthly or annual commits; we can model a 12-month commit with phased ramp.
3) Private (VPC/on-prem) is available if procurement/legal requires on-prem deployment or strict controls — typically later stage.

Payment & procurement notes:
- PO vs Card: We can accept standard POs for Dedicated/reserved contracts. Hosted on a pay-as-you-go basis can be billed to card or invoiced with a smaller minimum.
- Marketplace: We are listed on AWS Marketplace; if you prefer to purchase via the marketplace we can provide a quote that mirrors the committed pricing, though marketplace billing sometimes requires a different cadence.
- Documentation needed: completed SOW (attached template), PO number, and any vendor onboarding forms from Acme.

Attachments I've included: Redwood_SOW_template_v1.pdf (fill in scope and signatures) and a preliminary pricing summary for the pilot and a 12-month committed Dedicated projection (Redwood_pricing_summary_acme.xlsx). Also attached an excerpt of our SOC 2 report for procurement.

Next steps
- Samantha / Tom: confirm whether procurement prefers PO or AWS Marketplace for the pilot (we recommend PO for Dedicated).
- Marissa/Aditya: will build a recommended committed vs on-demand pricing model once we get a sense of preferred billing flow and target commit level.
- Dev/Aditya: follow up on security questions (SOC2, data residency) — flagged for procurement.

Proposed timeline:
- Pilot kick-off: week of Oct 26 (assuming procurement clears PO within 2–4 weeks).

Thanks — I’ll coordinate a short call with Sales Ops (Michael) if that helps unblock the PO process.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood-inference.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Subject: Re: Recap & Next Steps from Today’s Discovery — Procurement and Packaging Options

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers from procurement side:
- PO is our preferred route for anything above $25k/year; card is only for proof-of-concept/one-off purchases under that threshold.
- Marketplace would be ideal because it speeds vendor management for our legal team, but finance will need the committed pricing mirrored there.
- Estimated procurement lead time is ~6–8 weeks for a new vendor PO (vendor onboarding + contract review).

A few asks from our side before we loop Legal/Procurement:
1) Can you confirm whether committed Dedicated pricing requires a minimum term (12 months typical) and whether there are ramp clauses?
2) For the pilot on Hosted, can we get an invoice-based option (PO) for the pilot run — that would help us keep procurement moving while we evaluate Dedicated.
3) Any additional evidence you can provide on data residency and SOC2 controls would help speed IT Security review.

If you can send a short doc that maps Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private to procurement implications (billing flow, expected paperwork, estimated timeline) that would be perfect.

Thanks,
Samantha
Senior Procurement Manager | Acme Corp
samantha.reynolds@acme.com

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood-inference.com>

Date: 2026-10-13T14:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap & Next Steps from Today’s Discovery — Procurement and Packaging Options

Hi Samantha —

Quick answers to your questions: 
1) Committed Dedicated pricing: typical minimum term is 12 months for reserved capacity. We support monthly or annual billing for the commit; ramp clauses are common and we can model a phased ramp (e.g., 40% commit first 3 months, 70% next 3 months, 100% by month 7) to match usage growth.
2) Pilot on Hosted with PO: yes — we can invoice the pilot to a PO (we’ll need the PO number and standard vendor onboarding form). That lets you run the pilot while the larger PO for Dedicated is processed.
3) Security & residency: attaching SOC2 excerpt and a one-page data residency summary. Dev can provide a short note on network architecture for the hosted flow if you need it for IT review.

I’ve attached a short comparison table in the pricing workbook outlining procurement implications:
- Hosted: fastest onboarding, lower paperwork, invoice or card for pilot, pay-as-you-go; good for PoC.
- Dedicated: predictable performance and cost, supports PO and committed billing, requires SOW + PO + vendor onboarding; best for production.
- Private: full control (VPC/on-prem), higher ops lead time; typically used for regulated workloads — longer procurement cycle.

Michael — could you weigh in on typical PO terms we accept and confirm whether we can mirror committed pricing on AWS Marketplace for this account?

Thanks,
Aditya
